普通的爆炸在采矿和陷阱制作方面有它们的用途,但它们破坏一切的欲望限制了它们的应用.你认为你已经解决了这个问题,通过把一般爆炸产生的冲击波转化为神秘场中的涟波,将所有触及到的物体粉碎为要素.
炼金炸药所破坏的方块将会掉落晶化源质而非一般的物品.所有因爆炸而死的生物也会有类似的命运,尽管它们依旧掉落常规物品.
让一个灵气节点去承受这种爆炸所产生的力场绝对不是一个好主意...

虽然针对无生命物质的炼金变换已经足够简单,但鲜有活体在被实施炼金术之后生还的案例.你在最近的研究中应用了一些不一样的思路-你只是简单用炼金术加速了它们自然生长的过程,而非尝试去直接"修改"它们.
通过把普通食用作物的种子浸入浓缩的光,水,土的混合精华之中,植物可以以令人震惊的速度生长.但很不幸,这个过程是把双刃剑;这些植物毫无例外地在它们结出果实前就已经死亡了.
大多数植物可以通过炼金栽培的产物进行进一步的繁衍,但这种方式对小麦的生长没有效果.

在炼金栽培的成功之后,将类似的方法应用于动物上似乎是一个符合逻辑的选择.向一个鸡蛋提供温暖而原始的生命能量将保证鸡蛋中的胚胎在破壳时能够存活.
但更好的消息是,通过对鸡的初期生长过程的限制,你好像已经解决了作物快速老化的灾难性问题.

进行了一些研究后,你发现了方法强化这个珍珠.另一方面,你知道即便是这些碎片也有使用的潜力,所以你想出了种更有效获取它们的方法.

你成功在贪婪箱子上做了些改进,将其作用对象转为开箱子的人而不是邻近的容器.通过缓和所使用的珍珠,易物箱子被注入了对"交易"而不是窃取的渴望.它是如此的迫不及待以至于一被打开就会试着交易物品.
不过你事先准备了一些漏洞,让你能在§l潜行§r时直接查看箱内的物品而不是交易.另外,箱子不会与它无法识别的人交易,默认为放置者,

但其他人也能用法杖来将自己添加进识别对象.
法杖也可以用于设置箱子所要交易的物品.默认情况下,它会取走一切它觉得有价值的东西而给你它觉得无价值的那些-事实上,装上了符文白名单和黑名单也是如此的,不同之处就在于这些名单改变了它的评估.

很久以来,魔法的实践家们都尝试着用魔法给伙伴带来便利.而在钓鱼这方面,渔夫们都爱吹嘘附魔.
但不可靠的附魔结果让人难以满意.为什么不试试魔法呢?将你所发现的注魔法附魔运用到垂钓之中,说不定就能让他们眼前一亮呢.

有时手写的指令并不能完全表达你想的东西...尤其是在你需要魔法时.
通过向普通的纸中注入Vis并印上金色的符文,你就能做出让你的设备按你所想而执行工作的附魔纸.
最平常的用途就是用来制作白名单和黑名单,它们用于指示奥术设备如贪婪箱子所能"看见"的物品.

你能在保持已写入配置不变的条件下将白名单变为黑名单(或者反过来).
你也能从一张名单中将过滤配置复制到另一张名单上(种类不限),只需将它们俩放入奥术工作台即可.配置信息就会拷入另一张名单(当然这个过程不会消耗第一张名单).

§l §n附魔§r
附魔纸也能装订成书.用这些书所制成的书架能提供四倍于原版书架的附魔加成(对附魔台而言),因此只需4个这样的书架就可以在附魔台进行30级的附魔了.

你对于贪婪珍珠和末影人恐吓之间联系的研究终于有了回报.你制作了一个指环,戴在手上时,它就会钩住末影生物制造的隐形的瞬移路径.附近发生的每次瞬移(不管是瞬移来还是瞬移走)都会被这些钩子强行撕扯,重伤瞬移的末影生物.
它的能力需要有§8Perditio§0Vis的供应源(如法杖).每当有生物因它受到伤害时就会抽取少量的Vis.

§l §n符文护盾§r
你对于§l符文护盾升级§r的研究应该能用在这个指环上,你若能承担得起注魔成本就能让它能提供符文护盾.

如果能数清楚一片区域内的生物和实体数想必会很有用,用§2Terra§0源质强化过的水晶之脑便能做到这一点-它兼有对生命§r魔力与建筑方块物质的亲和力-使它更能胜任这一工作.
当它所能感应范围内存在指定实体时,它就能输出红石信号.数量越多,信号越强(最强为15).你也可以将它设定为只计算成年动物,或幼年动物.
设备所检验的区域由周围的方块所决定.如果一侧有空气或草,

那么该方向的检测范围就会增大一些.而如果所有的方向都是开阔的,设备就会处在检测区域的中心.如果仅有顶,北,东是开阔的,设备就会处在检测区域底部的西南角上.(默认的区域大小是11x11x11的范围.)§l §n兽灵之眼§r
你想要指定实体的种类,便利用现有的水晶之眼做了些改进,使其能记忆一种生物,它的灵魂,或是形态特征.手持它右击生物就能记忆,之后将兽灵之眼放入设备即可.
它也能做成用于观察人类(玩家)的眼睛,无论是指定的个人或是任意的人都可以.记忆的方法和前面所讲的相同.如果要记忆自身,手持它按住shift右键几秒钟即可.
从蕴魔石获取的碎片只是矿物中魔力的一部分.经过对该处理过程的一些细微调整,你就能从原矿中提取出更多潜在的魔力,虽然是以裂片的形式.

你计划着制作一个统一检测源质制造与分配的系统.而它的核心-或者叫神经中枢-就是源质聚核.
这个系统有很大的潜力但它的起点却比较简单.聚核会检测源质罐子的内容物然后根据综合情况转化为红石信号.尽管如此,作为源质读取器来使用的话它可以方便地反映出所有罐子的源质总量,而不是单个.
首先需要制作出聚核的关键组件,它需要放置在水之魔晶的上方,而水之魔晶要放在一个青金石块的上方.

青金石块周围要有水环绕着,水池则要用银树木板圈起.
源质聚核必须最后放置.
建成聚核后,用水晶之眼来指定源质罐子.一个水晶之眼可以指向多个罐子:任何与初始位置相邻的以及用类似方式相连接的罐子均会被检测.用设定好的眼睛右击聚核来使用.空手右击则会移除已有的水晶之眼.
通常来说,最多可以检测12个罐子,使用一个水晶之眼.

在多方块结构里,若银树木板上放置了水之魔晶则会增加上限.每个增加8个罐子以及1个水晶之眼的上限.每个魔晶也会增加一组罐子离聚核最远的有效距离.
注意尽管源质读取器不能直接放置在源质聚核方块的下方,放置在多方块结构中的水方块的下方也是有效的,你也可以使用远程比较器来读取源质信息.

§l §n源质库§r
你发现源质聚核能像对罐子那样获取一个源质库的总量.甚至不需多加校正.你觉得这一天一定会来的.有志者事竟成!

完成了源质聚核后,你开始将目光转向一排排的罐子,是时候让你的源质储存库变为分配中心了.
下方装有源质聚合器的聚核会成为邻近§l源质魔镜§r的源质供应端(当然也包括其他设备如符文祭坛).聚核抽取的源质来自它所监管的有效容器(如源质罐子).
这样一来你就能在一个地方统计源质,安置魔镜,以及进行注魔.
你相信未来还能用它做到更多.
通过在饕餮之口的基础上做些改进,你现在可以抑制它对特定物品的"食欲".手持法杖,符文白名单或黑名单右击深究之口,然后根据你的需要放入白名单或黑名单.

有了核心镶饰台,现在你能拓展合成核心的能力了.
§l无偿:§r 这项升级使得核心的基本运行不消耗Vis.(打开合成栏以及合成物品时都不会消耗额外的魔力.)
§l储存:§r 在使用这种升级的核心合成之后,合成栏内留下的任何物品都会被储存在与核心相连的异次元中.
§l置换:§r 有此项升级的核心在使用者需要时会自动装上法杖.无论核心是在背包还是手袋中都可以生效.
(只要按下核心所对应的键位就可以自动安装.)

不管你离家多远,合成的需求总是没完没了.油的合成还需要你到处都带着工作台,现在你找到了更简便的解决方法.
这个法杖核心能用于制造奥术工作台所能合成的一切物品(不管是普通合成还是奥术合成).安装核心的法杖将会提供合成所需的源质.
你只要装好核心再用法杖右击即可开始合成.如果装着核心的法杖在工具栏里,你也可以按'%s'键来打开合成.
当你打开合成栏的时候会消耗少量vis,每次合成奥术物品的时候也会消耗一些.(普通合成的物品不需要额外的vis.)

§l §n魔杖§r
尽管这个核心也能装在魔力手杖上面,但这类工具显然不适合奥术合成的精密工作.但它仍能进行普通的合成.

傀儡抑制器能将傀儡脚镣产生的作用升级.它的作用可不止是让傀儡在某个方块上停下脚步,而是让范围内的傀儡全部停止.
抑制器必须放在傀儡脚镣的上方.它只在脚镣被激活时生效.下方可以继续添加脚镣.连接的激活脚镣越多(最多为4个),作用范围就越大.

§l §n连接§r
若有傀儡连接到了该设备,它就会免疫傀儡抑制器的效果,而能像正常的那样继续活动.
你也可以让连接的傀儡变为唯一的作用目标.
用法杖右击抑制器就能切换它的模式.

为了最大化利用傀儡抑制器这样的神秘设备,你必须将傀儡连接到它们.手持绑定铃铛右击设备,就可以开始连接了.用绑定铃铛再次右击一个傀儡就能将它绑定到设备上.
当然,也有一些限制.尽管与设备的连接在任何距离都能保持,最大的生效范围还是有限的.其次,每个傀儡只能连接到一个设备.最后,一个设备最多连接6个傀儡.(当数量超出这个值时可能会发生意想不到的情况,

比如部分傀儡会像是没有被连接一样活动.)
如果你想切断一个设备所有的连接,只需在潜行时用铃铛右击(按住Shift).
潜行时右击一个方块即可移除铃铛已绑定的设备信息.
§o已更新目前所有支持傀儡连接的设备的研究笔记.§r

在傀儡升级的基础上,你开发出了一系列新的升级,用于增强傀儡工作台的和合成性能.
一次最多能安装4个升级,每个侧面一个.同种类型升级的效果可以叠加(除了混沌).
潜行时用法杖右击装有升级的那一侧即可移除升级.
§l风:§r 傀儡能将它的速度优势用于合成.傀儡速度越快,合成的也就越快.但使用该升级的傀儡更易疲倦,

这也就意味着需要更多的§8Fabrico§0源质来让其全速工作.
§l火:§r 傀儡能多记忆一个配方.相应的,工作台内可用的格子也会多出一套.每个工作台最多只能安装§l两个§r该种升级.
§l地:§r 傀儡能将它的力量优势用于合成.傀儡越强壮合成就越快.尽管加速效果稍弱于风的升级,但傀儡的耐力也会提升,不那么容易疲倦了.

§l混沌:§r 合成配方不再作为精准匹配而是以形状来确定.底部第一个槽里的物品如果在配方中,都会被当做一个占位符.傀儡会检查工作台含有的其他物品,以此来判断用其他物品之一来替换占位符是否能制作出所需的产物.
举例来说,在合成栏的一格中放入木棍,另一格放入羊毛,然后在下方最左边的槽中放入木棍,这样就能让傀儡合成所有颜色的羊毛了(前提是提供所需的染料).
这般模糊的逻辑也伴随着代价,使用该种升级的傀儡会更容易疲劳.

傀儡工作台让你能摆出合成配方,加上一些魔法的协助,即便是傀儡也能照着合成.
对你蠢萌的傀儡来说还有许多配方太过复杂.除非合成是2x2的或者所有的原料都是一样的,不然你就需要§l高级傀儡§r了.
首先在9个格子中设定好合成配方,底部的格子中提供所需的材料.然后对着工作台放置一个装有§l空置§r傀儡运转核心的傀儡,命令傀儡从中容器取出合成产物(右击傀儡设置).用傀儡使铃铛告诉傀儡应在何处放置新的物品.

注意在这里只有原版工作台可合成的才有效.即便是你最高级的傀儡也无法了解奥术合成使用魔力的原理.但你觉得这样也足够了.
若要让傀儡专心工作提升效率,你可以在附近放置一个装有§8Fabrico§0源质的罐子.这将会起到很大帮助,尤其是傀儡在很长时间内持续合成物品,它们可能会有些'瞌睡'的情况下.真够懒的.

§l §n高级傀儡§r
如你所愿,高级傀儡能进行更复杂的合成.它们能使用3x3的配方以及不止一种原料.

§l §n傀儡镣铐§r
如果傀儡镣铐直接放在工作台下面,那么,当它被激活时,傀儡将不会在工作台上合成任何物品.它们不一定完全停止(只要它们别自己踩上去),但是,这意味着它们可以继续从工作台中清空指定物品.
当管理多个傀儡或傀儡拒绝始终站在一个位置时，这可能是有用的.

§n混沌升级解锁特性§rthaumcraft:textures/items/golem_upgrade_entropy.png:0:0:255:255:0.0625如果相连的傀儡安装了混沌升级,那就意味着它会忽略物品的损伤,NBT数据以及检测矿物辞典来判断它所合成的东西.(这取决于傀儡是否能移动物品.)
只会影响到合成产物,而不会影响到合成使用的原料.或许进一步的研究能解决这个问题.
§n秩序升级解锁特性§rthaumcraft:textures/items/golem_upgrade_order.png:0:0:255:255:0.0625当合成中产生了残留物品并且无法当做合成原料(比如合成蛋糕中的空桶),通常物品就会被合成傀儡扔到一边.如果傀儡安装了这项升级,它就会将残留的物品放入工作台(如果空间允许的话)

有时你疑惑饕餮箱子是否和真正的暴食相关,或者你能否将其变为一种简单稳定的自动功能.你所知的仅仅是它在吞食物品时发出的声音....
尽管你难以发觉自己对这些东西的认知能力,但你的研究显示你或许还能给类似的物体注入其他的"需求".这是从基础的饕餮迈向原始的贪婪的一小步,要将其运用起来还需要其他一些特殊部件的发明.

贪婪箱子会窃取邻近容器内的物品.比如放入邻近容器中50%的物品都会被放入它的内部.如果你用法杖右击,则可以改变这个行为让其每次取的数量更多或更少,维持固定存量,或只取走超出给定数量的物品.你也可以选择抽取物品的来源方向.
他不能从其下方的漏斗中抽取物品,也不能从另一个在它这里抽取物品的贪婪箱子窃取物品.
你正在研究如何让箱子只抽取特定的物品(某种过滤机制)但

这应该是个好的开始.
同时,对于这个§l珍珠§r的其他发现也很有趣.普通的末影珍珠会将你传送到它落下的位置,但这一个则会作用于其附近的物品.或许你应该带着它到处转转.§o你可能会学习到些什么.§r

§l §n附魔纸§r
利用符文白名单和黑名单,你就能改变箱子抽取物品的种类和具体抽取数量,让你设置它应该抓取的物品.

你将饕餮箱子的能力提取出来并用在了一种能装在其他容器的洞上.触碰到饕餮之口或是离得近的任何物品都会被吸入它所附着的容器中.
开始时,先将一个黑曜石放在饕餮箱子上方.然后将另三个黑曜石放置在箱子侧面(不需要在箱子下方放置).最后,用装有便携式洞穴核心的法杖右击箱子上的方块.
每个黑曜石能产生一个饕餮之口.饕鬄箱子和黑曜石都会被消耗掉;幸运的是,法杖和法杖核心不会消耗.

为了有效管理你的储存,你需要的不仅仅是一个列表,而是一种方法来取出你所储存的东西.除了傀儡还有什么更好的方法呢?
为了让你的配送系统如预期那样运行你还需要一些东西.首先你得有一个有效的库存系统(包括至少一个读取了容器的记录桌),一个能与储存容器交互的傀儡,一个合适的卸货点以便傀儡放下取出的物品,提供订单的途径以及让订单转为傀儡理解范畴的方式.为了实现后两个,你发明了一些新的设备.

可以使用多个卸货点,每个对应一个或多个§l填充§r核心的傀儡,卸货点就是傀儡的绑定点.卸货点可以选在任何一处,但如果是一个容器的话,它§l必须能快速排空§r物品否则就可能造成堵塞.综合考虑来说,物品格栅配合魔镜要优于一个箱子 - 或许也会有人选择将物品直接送往提交订单的地方.
每个被记录桌读取的容器都应该有至少一个填充傀儡连接(通过傀儡使铃铛),这些傀儡也不能连接到其他容器不然就有可能发生预料之外的情况.最好将容器内的物品整理以便在指定物品类型的情况下快速配送少走弯路.

接下来,在附近放置一个§l傀儡指示器§r然后将填充傀儡连接到它,使用§l傀儡连接铃铛§r即可.每个傀儡指示器最多能处理6个傀儡.这些傀儡必须绑定到同一个卸货点,指示器只能控制休息点(当它们未搬运物品时所在的地点)距离5格以内的傀儡.
就和记录桌一样,指示器必须连接到库存核心(用法杖右击)并且距离可以通过核心附近的秩序魔晶来提升.允许的指示器数量取决于安装的

§l记忆方块§r数,因此你需要安装至少1个.
要让记忆方块安装成功,它必须放置在核心下方2格起7x2x7的范围内,并且必须紧邻琥珀方块或琥珀砖块(比如核心下方的那个).用法杖右击核心就会显示当前使用的以及最大的记忆槽数量.

最后所需的就是§l申请台§r了.和记录桌一样,它会显示整个储存系统的内容物.这也就是你提交订单的地方.
左击列表中的物品来增加征订的数量,右击减少.按住shift来移动整组,或ctrl来一次性移动10单位物品.使用左侧的一栏或按住alt/option来请求多于储存量的数目.
申请台的需求类似于傀儡指示器:一个专用的记忆方块,连接至核心,并且可以通过秩序魔晶提升连接距离.此外它还需要供应§8Ordo§0源质(通过Vis中继器 ).

将一个§l计数盒§r指向申请台就会使盒子根据当前征求的物品输出红石信号.
最后提醒:傀儡并不能完美地适应订单的变动,因此如果你在傀儡已经取多了的情况下减少征求量,它们只会将多出的扔在地上.最好再想办法将这些物品放回原位.

§l §n聚合魔镜§r
通过GUI中的"魔镜"按钮与水晶之眼,聚合魔镜可以取代标准魔镜用于物品输入.

将库存核心周围的普通书架替换成另外几种,就可以提升它所能读取的格数(远多于81格).
每个§l附魔书架§r(由附魔纸制成)可提供216格(相当于8个箱子的容量).
每个§l蕴魔书架§r则可以提供486格(相当于18个箱子).和附魔书架类似,它也能用于提升附魔台的附魔等级.它的附魔加成相当于原版书架的8倍.

记录桌的限制就在于它只能检测一种类型的容器,且容器必须被放置在其后.记录之眼就摆脱了这个约束.
它使用§l水晶之眼§r指向邻近的容器来设置类型.一次最多能使用5个眼睛.
使用方法很简单,将它放在记录桌的上方再用准备好的水晶之眼右击即可.空手右击则可取下上一次装入的水晶之眼.
用你准备好的水晶之眼右击它.空手右击可以移除最后插入的水晶之眼.

你所有的物品越多,要管理它们就越难.当对象是一群不同的箱子甚至更多时,计数盒也会捉襟见肘.你所需的是一个集中式的储存管理系统.应对这个需求就有了Inventarium(库存的拉丁语,下译为库存).
为了建成这个结构,库存核心必须放在一个秩序魔晶的上方,秩序魔晶要放在一个琥珀方块或琥珀砖块的上方.还要按照后几页所示的图摆好书架.
核心必须最后放置.
库存本身不包含任何物品但它可以去许多容器相关联.对于任何直接指向库存核心或八个书架之一(或用远程比较器连接核心)的计数盒,都会根据所有关联容器的内容物输出红石信号.<LINE>若要将容器绑定至库存,你需要至少一个§l容器记录桌§r.这个蕴含魔力的设备将会记录它附近特定对象的内容物,并将信息完全输送给库存.它只会检测一种指定的容器.

而在它面前最早发现的容器就会限定该种类.有效范围是以记录桌为中心7x7x7的区域.
注意每个记录桌都需要稳定供应§8Ordo§0源质,你可以用Vis中继器来实现持续供给.每个库存核心最多支持的记录桌数量起初都是1.以核心为中心7x7x7区域内放置的每个秩序魔晶都可以增加1个上限.这也会增加记录桌距离核心最远的有效距离.

区域内每个书架使库存所能检测的最大容量增加81格.(相当于每个书架3个标准的箱子.)以下情况容器不会被部分检测:如果它的总容量大于有效的容量,整个容器为非检测对象.
要将一个记录桌连接到库存核心,只需用法杖右击记录桌.核心必须在10格以内(每个秩序魔晶额外增加8格).

如果记录桌位于做个核心的范围内,它就会连接到最近的那一个.若要让它连接至另一个,你就要先用法杖右击来标记那个核心.
用法杖右击核心也会提醒你库存当前的使用量,最大库存容量以及记录桌数.

你所设计的沙漏在信号延时和红石脉冲的产生上来说很实用,但它还缺些什么比如重复工作的能力.并且有时候你需要它在被激活时从零开始计时,但对普通沙漏而言这显然是不可能的,因为它们会用一端的沙子继续计时.
为了弥补这些缺陷,你用魔法赋予了沙漏反复倒置和将沙子瞬间移回上端(重新计时)的能力.如果你有意,它亦可将沙子移至底端,提前结束计时而不从沙漏输出信号

(亦会根据设置停止循环).
此外,还有多种不同的信号模式.§l脉冲§r模式是标准的.§l持续§r模式意味着在沙子下落时沙漏会一直输出信号.§l交替模式§r与其类似但只会在50%的情况下输出信号.§l反脉冲§r模式类似于持续模式,不过在沙漏倒置的时候会有短暂的间隔不输出信号(如果设置了循环的话).§l禁用§r意味着不会输出任何信号.
沙漏收到信号的反应(除了左右面以外的任意一侧)也能改变.默认情况下,沙漏每次收到信号时都会颠倒.

另外的选项就是让它仅在有信号或无信号时运行.它也能设置为完全无视红石信号.
最后,相比之前,现在你可以每次调节5单位的时间并且它的最长计时也比红石沙漏要长.你需要用法杖来这么做(右击);因为这可不是插根棍子就能调整的机械装置.

尽管魔镜很适合将物品从一处送到另一处，但它们只能成对地连接。一个系统如果使用多个魔镜从不同的地方将物品输出到同一处的话，那么成本也未免太高了。你对于虚空的了解和虚空金属性质的研究或许能起到些帮助。
§l聚合魔镜§r是一面特制的“单向”镜子，它只能接收而不能吐出物品。若要将它连接到其他的镜子，你还需要给其镶上一个§l水晶之眼§r（右击）。如果水晶之眼指向的位置是已经配对过的魔镜的话（任何维度的任何位置）

聚合魔镜就会寻找联系着配对魔镜的跨维细流，然后通过汇流点将物品传送到目标位置。
在潜行时用法杖右击即可移除魔镜上的水晶之眼。让魔镜能在虚空中利用连接点的关键部件就是§l汇流圆盘§r。圆盘本身占据了魔镜的大部分框架，制作所用的虚空金属也让它能以一种特殊的方式与玻璃结合，或许这也能帮助它应付虚空那些中充满了混沌的细流。
汇流圆盘初始的制作成本较高，但只要有了一个，持续生产就不难了。因此建议保留一个以作备用。

到目前为止,将多个申请台与单个库存连接起来的效用有限.所申请的物品与任何特定的申请台无关,更不用说专门用于配送给它们了.现在你已经找到了一种方法来利用魔镜之间的跨维细流,是时候改变了.
如果你的配送傀儡被设置为在连接的§l分发魔镜§r(直接或间接)中丢下物品,并且此魔镜与傀儡指示器连接到相同的库存核心,那么魔镜可以将物品传送至靠近申请台的另一魔镜.
用你的法杖右击以连接分发魔镜与库存核心.

在库存核心附近放置秩序魔晶可以拓展最大有效范围.每个分发魔镜必须安装§l记忆方块§r.(查阅"供与求"以了解如何做到这一点.)
魔镜连接后,你必须使用申请台GUI中的 “魔镜” 按钮以指定每个申请台的目标魔镜.标准魔镜或聚合魔镜都可以作为申请台的输出位置.
请注意,发送到分发魔镜并且未指定目的地的物品将被分发魔镜拒绝并吐出,所以请确保所有的申请台都有指定的输出魔镜.(你可能还需要一个故障保护装置来
拾取掉落物品并将它们带到默认目的地或将它们丢弃.)

在研究下界之核所用的符文时,火注魔水晶之脑的另一项能力初露头角.当它的能量潜入周围生物的精神中时,就会灌输一种强烈的情绪.
在此之上你做出了一个能吸引周围生物的设备.所灌输的情绪让这些生物忽视周围的环境,即便途中会从高处落下也要向它靠近.
尽管制作时使用了符文黑曜石,但产物却截然不同.不能用于下界之核的构建.

事实上就其自身而言,用已知的黑曜石还不能达到你想要的效果.幸运的是,古人们留下了一些可用的工艺品.
要让它生效,你需要将石头作为一根竖直§l黑曜石图腾§r柱(最少使用2块图腾)的一部分来放置.这样一来水平方向范围内的敏感生物就会被其所吸引,竖直的范围由柱子的高度决定.(最大为向上或向下4格).
水平的范围可以扩大,如果附近有§4Fames§0源质罐子的话.
用你的§l法杖§r轻击来激活它.

不同的生物对塞壬的呼唤反应也不同.大部分会盲目的走向它.其他的如末影人则会陷入混乱,甚至在快要摔落的时候试着逃离,但这也是短暂的.事实上,受其影响的§l末影人§r会§l瞬移得更近§r而不是更远.
部分生物对它完全免疫,包括你的傀儡,一些强大的生物,以及头脑简单的史莱姆.
如果一个生物所在的区域内有多个塞壬之饵,它就会转向最强的那一个.图腾柱越高,塞壬之饵就越强.

将强度使用得巧妙的话,也能让生物按你所想的路线被吸引而来.
塞壬之饵不会永久的吸引生物的注意力.如果一段时间内它无法接近石头,那么效果就会消失,再次吸引该生物就又要消耗一些时间了.最后,忙于战斗的生物能摆脱它的蛊惑.

在近期的实验中,你发现火源质强化的水晶之脑似乎会持续吸取能量(并且快速烧蚀自身).这股能量让你追溯到了下界.如果你能找到什么与下界之火密切联系又能与它共存的东西,或许就能做出一个"下界之核",利用源质来构建岩浆和下界方块.
§l灰烬之心§r或许能胜任.进一步的研究显示,它与烈焰人这类地狱怪物甚至与它们的生成有着联系.

显然你需要用某种方法来驱动并控制下界之核.最终你做出了§l符文黑曜石§r.除了用于包围下界之核,这些符文还要按照指定的方式搭建好(见下一页).
不同的符文有不同的功能.图中所示的任意基础符文都可以被特殊符文所替换.某种符文数量越多,其效果就越强.如果只是用基础的符文,该设备的运行将会十分缓慢,并且只会生成地狱岩和零星的岩浆.

当符文全都安装完毕后,用你的法杖轻触下界之核就能启动它了.你也能再次右击来关闭它,但每次启动都会消耗法杖中的vis.
运行时,下界之核必须用§cIgnis§0源质供应.它也需要附近有源质罐子以抽取源质.所需的源质类型及数量取决于工作中的符文.基础的符文只会消耗Ignis和Terra.
生成的下界方块会出现在结构下方两格9x9x9的区域内.

当这种红晶接收到红石信号时,它会向特定方向输出一个满强度的信号.如果用于传输信号的是其他红晶,那么它的有效强度就会在衰减为强度14之前许多格保持为强度15,之后就会像普通红石信号一样每格衰减强度1.
弱化红晶则是个例外,它会将信号强度立刻减至14甚至更低.
增幅红晶只会接收从输出方向的反侧来的信号.

钝化红晶的特殊构造使得弱些的红石信号无法穿透它继续传递.幸运的是,它的构造是魔法的并能按照你的意愿调整.实际上,钝化红晶总会输出一个小于等于你设定强度的信号,若输入信号小于你的设定强度则不会输出信号.
要改变所需的最小强度,只需用法杖右击钝化红晶的中心.

这类红晶让你能限制其输出信号的强度.在设备对不同信号强度反应不同时很实用.它仍能输出比上限低些强度的信号,所以你可能需要配合其他的东西来使用,比如增幅红晶或是红石火把.
用你的法杖右击弱化红晶的中心就能改变它的上限了.

现在你终于能踏足通过魔镜发现的奇妙领域,创造远距离传输的网络,你需要能有效控制那些特性各异的元素.为何要将资源浪费在制造和用镜子传送物品上,明知这会堆满箱子和减缓传输速度?
通过改进共鸣红晶,使其振动接近于世界间那虚空的飘忽不定的状态,你就做出了镜像红晶.它能通过绑定邻近的镜子向镜子另一侧的镜像红晶传输红石信号.
为了输送或接收信号,它必须连接到一个镜子.手持它右击镜子即可.之后将它放在距离镜子8格以内的一处.当然,你也需要在另一边将另一个红晶绑定到对应的镜子.

§l §n源质魔镜§r
除了标准的魔镜以外,镜像红晶也能连接到一面源质魔镜.当普通魔镜在使用时这应该算是更好的选择了.

在你制作各种红晶的初始阶段,你试验了各种元始源质.风源质显露出了独特而有趣的振荡能量,但因其强度太弱不能投入实际运用.进一步研究后,你现在能将那种能量聚集在特定方向上,使其能被远距离接收.
共鸣红晶通过空气和类似的物体来直线传输红石信号,直到其被另一个共鸣红晶接收到.因此两个红晶必须面对面放置(若一个附着在方块底部,

另一个就必须附着在方块顶端并且位于其下方).
信号最多可以跨越15格传输.强度在这过程中没有衰减,就好像两个水晶相邻放置的一样.

你发现某些材料一旦通过特殊方法结晶化就能变得更易于用魔法控制.新的晶体结构会重组其构造,而在某些情况下,可将信号印于其上.
这是你在研究红石粉时的发现.最终你得到了红石水晶-或者称为§l红晶§r-在调整选择方向时更简单.它能放在方块的任何一面.用你的法杖右击红晶的某个方向就能增加或移除与邻近方向的连接.
除了将信号传递给相邻红晶方块之外,它也会将信号传递给转角处没有直接接触的红晶,前提是它们都附着在同一方块上并且相邻区域没有阻隔.automagy:textures/gui/redcrystal-corner.png:0:0:255:208:.5

红石拥有许多不寻常的特性.它传输信号和构建电路的能力让人们认为它是某种平凡的科技.实际上,红石的力量正是各种科技所依赖的基础.然而,精通奥术魔法的人深知它的特性对各种魔法来说都是极其重要的,活塞可能就是个最知名的例子.
因为这些原因,红石常被看做为魔法与科技之间的天然桥梁.它确实是,但神秘使们知道远不止这些:从最基础的层面来讲,红石完全不能算作平凡的材料.

即使其作为复杂电路或是机器设备的一部分而运作时,进一步的研究说明它的特性更接近于魔法.
你打算充分利用这种奇妙的物质.至此,你设计了些助你在日常中更好地运用"红石逻辑"的简单设备.
你确定进一步的研究能产生更大的发现.实际上,这或许是完整的新神秘学科的基础,它能让神秘使们实现更智能的自动化.你觉得应该称它为§5自动化魔法§r.

§l §n红石转换火把§r
红石火把对红石信号的转化能力很有用,但你发现它会在两态之间转变.即便最弱的信号输入了火把附着的方块也会使其熄灭,并且当其亮着时总会发出满强度的红石信号.但若你想要的是真正意义上的转化信号又怎么样?不仅仅是15转为0,也包括10转为5,3转为12,以此类推?
你利用基础的神秘原理做出了个更加有序的,不仅仅是15和0强度之间变换的红石火把.

§l §n沙漏§r
红石沙漏是个简单实用的装置,让你能调节红石信号传递的时间.
当其被激活时(通过右击或者红石信号),沙漏就会颠倒使得沙子漏下.当其完全漏完时就会输出一个红石脉冲.如果红石比较器的后侧贴着沙漏,它就会在沙子下落时输出一个强度持续增大的信号.
沙漏从左右两侧输出信号.其他面接收信号.
用法杖或木棍右击沙漏即可调节时长.
尽管计时十分精确但只能以5秒为增量调节,最高不能超过60秒,但你知道这个设备将成为更好发明的基石.

信号能反映出箱子内物品的多少然而红石比较器的放置经常会妨碍到其他事情.考虑到这个,你发明了远程比较器.它以一个容器的储存状态为基础输出信号,就像红石比较器那样,但它不一定要贴着容器放置.它也能作用于一些普通比较器无法检测的容器,包括许多神秘学相关的.
当然,还有必要需要告诉它应检测哪一个设备.幸运的是,你发现的晶体魔法能起到帮助.

一个水晶之眼能用于让特定的神秘设备监测其他坐标的对象.用眼睛右击需要监测的方块就能指定位置.之后,只需将设定好的眼睛放入设备提供的槽中即可.
在指定坐标系中监测设备的距离有一个限制.该限制默认是20格但部分设备可能还有其他要求.

不幸的是,将它们重组为碎片实为难事.因此制造一个碎片会比粉碎它消耗更多的Vis.

将透镜装在计数盒上就能改变它在目标位置检测物品的方式.
装有§l零散§r透镜的盒子会检测区域内散落的物品而不是容器中的.
§l产物§r透镜则会让盒子了解目标方块可能会掉落的物品.(标准结果以及精准采集的都会纳入考虑.)在目标含有特殊方块时这种输出信号的方法或许也不错.

能了解一个箱子内东西的总量多少的确不错,但事实上你更想知道特定的东西有多少.循着这个想法,你最终设计出了计数盒.
将它对着一个容器放置(类似放置漏斗).然后向其中放入一张符文白名单或黑名单.它就会根据你指定的条件来输出红石信号.信号会从计数盒的后方输出.
A你也可以将一个§l远程比较器§r放在盒子顶部,设置好水晶之眼,

再放入比较器.比较器就会终止其原本的功能,成为向计数盒传递物品信息的媒介.
如果一个计数盒读取的是另一个计数盒,那么信息就会从第二个计数盒的目标获取.如果它的目标还是一个计数盒,那么它就会转运它目标的信息,以此类推.通过这种方法链接计数盒以及远程比较器,就能从很远的距离外读取容器信息.

你已经掌握了如何给箱子注入贪婪的念头,在此之上制作一个新的箱子就显得轻而易举了.
吝物箱子会评估其中物品的价值,阻止它们被取出.你仍然可以直接打开并随意的取出物品,但傀儡,漏斗以及其他大部分自动化的方法都无法取出§l最后一叠§r的指定物品.
箱子会试着从每种物品中分离出一个.或许它觉得这样才能保有这些物品,
但这种行为的真正目的却是:让自动化在保留余量的前提下尽可能地存取其中的物品.

作为一名在各地间忙于飞行的神秘使，漫长的路途也需要给奥法缰绳提供充足的补给，这太麻烦了。现在，你有了更好的方法。
通过结合你在神秘学领域与产能节点的知识，你可以将其运用到通过隔空传输Potentia源质上。在源质源头与目标对象之间建立并维持连接会让你疲惫不堪，但注入了风源质的水晶之脑更能胜任这项工作。
用其搭建的§l奥法尖塔§r在建造时也需要满足一些条件才能生效。

首先需要制作2个§l奥法能量柱§r方块和1个§l奥法控制器§r.还需要1个錾制石英块和1个神秘块.
然后,各个部件必须正确放置.錾制石英块在底部,神秘块在顶部,能量柱和控制器在两者之间随意顺序摆放(无间隔).神秘块上方必须有空间使其能直视天空.所有的部分都摆放完毕后,用你的法杖右击控制器.

尖塔可以作用在很大一片区域内。只要尖塔有足够的源质并且有§6Aer§0魔力的驱动，范围内任何装备着且装有罐子的奥法缰绳都会有稳定供应的Potentia源质。用源质管道连接到§l控制器§r来提供Potentia源质。<LINE>有效范围可通过向控制器稳定供应Aer源质来扩大。补充Potentia源质的速率则可以通过给其输入Volatus源质来提升。结构中的添加能量柱可以同时增大范围与速率。（最多6个能量柱，多余的不会有增益效果。）
用法杖右击控制器的一侧即可改变该侧可接收的源质类型。

对于生物检测方面的进步让你创造出了一种新符石:汲奶符石.装有该符石的渴饮储罐不会吸取附近流动的液体.而会沿着符石朝向的那一面搜寻可以取奶的奶牛.
尽管搜寻奶牛的速度可以通过§l狂饮符石§r来提升,真正的限制因素在于:不能在短时间内从同一头牛那儿取奶.

渴饮储罐能做的事可不仅仅是收集并储存几桶的流体.为了挖掘它的潜力,你开发了一系列符石和注入水之魔力的颜料.当这种"水之印泥"被塑造为正确的形状时就会产生特殊的效果,它能被印在石板上,然后装在渴饮储罐的一侧.
一个渴饮储罐最多能拥有六个符石,每个面一个.面的选择很重要,因为某些符石的效果是指向性的.

若要移除一个符石,只需在潜行时用法杖右击安装的那一侧.
目前能制作的符石及其效果如下:
§l虚空:§r 储罐会吸收远多于容量的流体.超出的部分将会被销毁.
§l泯灭:§r 储罐将会逐渐消耗(销毁)它所储存的一切流体.增加数量可以提升消耗速度.
§l虹吸:§r 流体将会从储罐中沿着符石的朝向输入另一个容器.
§l嫉妒:§r 储罐将会从指定方向的容器抽取流体

,每次抽取一桶的量.
§l节制:§r 储罐仅在受到红石信号时才会将流体吸入其中.
§l贮存:§r 储罐会避免自身流体被抽光.你可以用它来确保储罐总是存有定量的流体.
§l狂饮:§r 储罐吸取流体的速度加快.该种符石越多速度越快.
§l库容:§r 每个符石会使储罐的流体容量提升16桶.

在原有的基础上稍加改动,驱使着饕餮箱子的饥饿之魔力也能让一个特制的储罐"吸取"与其接触的液体.
只有能被桶装起的液体才能被吞入,但即便是流动的液体也能让它有所反应.储罐能吸收从目标方块到本体之间相连的同种液体.这样一来,不需要移动储罐就能吸收完一个小池塘.
液体也能通过一般的方法来输入或输出储罐,

比如用桶或特定的傀儡.
如果紧邻水源方块放置,它能无限地从中吸水.

测量容器内的空区是个简单活儿,但涉及到Vis的种类和数量就是另一回事了.如何解决?就需要Vis读取器了.
从源质罐子到坩埚再到灵气节点,它会根据测定对象的Vis组成来输出红石信号.它甚至能读取法杖的Vis,前提是法杖放在了合适的设备上.
它有两种工作方式.最简单的就是直接放在要读取的对象的下方.另一种就是将一个远程比较器放在读取器上方,再将它的水晶之眼连接到目标位置.

比较器就会终止其原本的功能,成为向读取器传递Vis信息的媒介.
用你的法杖右击Vis读取器就能打开设置界面.
§l§n设置§r
Vis读取器输出的信号强度由它的设置和检测的源质决定.信号强度的标准类似比较器的容器检测:容器已满时强度15,空时强度0,其余的在之间变化.你可以放入§l罐子标签§r来过滤源质类型.
§l反转模式:§r 空时输出满强度信号

而满时不输出信号,其余的状态则与默认的相反.
§l总计模式:§r 所有要素的计数总量与容量相比.
§l任意(高)模式:§r 计数量最大的要素量与容量相比.若是§l节点§r,详见下一页.
§l任意(低)模式:§r 计数量最小的要素量与容量相比.若是§l节点§r,详见下一页.
§l容量:§r 计为满信号强度的那个值.如果设为§l自动§r,Vis读取器就会根据所检测的对象自动

选择容量(若可行的话).
§l节点:§r 读取对象为节点时,容量设为§l自动§r,模式选择为§l任意§r时,容量就会由特定要素的最大检测值而不是所有要素的来决定.用于对比的要素就是相对于自身容量最少或最多的那种,而不是某刻要素量最多或最少的.(因此如果模式为§l任意(高)§r,某种要素占满50%,为10单位要素中的5单位,那么就会比40单位要素中10单位即25%占满的那种更优先,即使后者有更多的要素量.)

§l §n节点§r
当读取的目标是节点时,容量为§l自动§r,以及§l任意§r选定模式,之后的容量则为某个指定要素检测的最大值,而不是所有要素的最大值之和.而指定的要素则为相对自身容量最满或最少的那一种,而不是当前含量最高或最低的那一种.
(因此如果模式为§l任意(高)§r,某种要素含量5点,占50%,最大容量10点,就会优先于另一种含量10点,占25%,容量40点的,尽管后者的要素含量更高.)

§l §n源质聚核§r
有了源质聚核的帮助,源质读取器就能对许多罐子的源质总量立刻做出反应.也可以将源质读取器放在结构中的水下或使用远程比较器连接到聚核方块本身来检测.
源质读取器对聚合的检测类似于灵气节点.它根据罐子容量计算当前所含源质或标签指定源质的最大值.

§l §n注魔§r
你发现Vis读取器不仅能测量对象中源质的存量,还能在某个设备运行时算出其缺乏的源质量.至少,这个应该能用在注魔祭坛中.
它可以根据注魔是否进行以及进行的状态来输出红石信号.

缸中之脑的经验储存容量是有限的.尽管遗忘之石能将这些记忆提取出来,但没法在不损失旧有经验的前提下为新的经验腾出空间.为了解决这一问题,你创造了一种新的石头.
当一块§l灵魂之石§r放置在缸中之脑下端的遗忘之石旁边时,会从脑中抽取经验,存入灵魂之石自身中.
如果石头中储存的经验超过了缸中之脑的量,那么

遗忘之石就会改变运行的方向,转而从灵魂之石中向缸中之脑输送经验,除非后者被装满.
这个组合就能满足你对于增加缸中之脑储存容量的需求了,但这里的灵魂之石并没有解决便携性的问题.如果直接破坏就会损失一部分储存的经验,掉落剩下的.幸运的是,还有解决的方法.
灵魂之石在某种意义上来说算是多孔的疏松结构.记忆能缓慢渗入石头中,石头起到了类似于滤网的作用,这些经验会随着流动而凝聚起来.
最终,这种精华液将浓缩到足以装入其他的容器.

在石头的下方放置一个未标签的§l源质罐子§r(一两格以内-再往下的话流体就会失效了),之后"附魔精华液"就会滴入其中.这个罐子可以安全地转移到别处,或用§l安瓿§r装取其中的精华液以饮用.
要注意的是,除非有固体方块的阻隔,即便没有罐子流体也会缓慢地从灵魂之石中滴落.不得不说这样做实在是浪费.

A few tries later, and the binding of the demonic power to the crystal works with Aquasalus, Incendium, and Aether. In theory, a Nether Star can be used in place of a demon blood shard, but considering how hard those are to get a hold of... Magus has been thrilled with his new crystal, and I have started work on a new project with Tiberius as a surprise for Magus. His rituals as they stand are good, but I have had an idea to make them even better... I'm having a hard time sleeping tonight, so I might as well go over our idea and hope Magus doesn't read this. As it stands, the rituals only use life essence to run and are often "one-trick ponies." What I proposed to Tiberius is this: What would happen if one of the rituals was charged with alchemical power, costing reagent to give it new or stronger effects? We might get nothing, or something amazing. Time will tell which it is.

I managed to improve the catalyst even further by mixing in a gold nugget and the fragments of a bone into the strengthened catalyst, making it into a much more concentrated form, hence the name "Concentrated catalyst." With it, I have been able to infuse the imbued slates created in the blood altar with alchemical power, making it stronger then normal and able to construct devices to hold alchemical and magical energy. On the potion items, I can finally make all the forms of the power and lengthening catalysts, filling agents. By merging two of a catalyst with a Standard Binding Agent you can make the standard form of said catalyst, and then you can create the greater form of the catalyst by fusing two of the standard with a reagent(Incendium for power and Aquasalus for lengthening). Adding these to a potion is the same process as the mundane, place the potion and the ingredient in the stand with the catalyst of choice. Note: You don't need to teir up from normal to the greatest, you can jump strait to the greatest effect by mixing in a greater catalyst. Adding a better catalyst to an old potion does nothing for the effect, and is the same as if you added it to a potion that never had a catalyst added. The greater filling agent is able to resort six charges to a one effect potion, and is made by adding Aquasalus and magicalus to a Standard Filling Agent. The remainder of my time has been spent brewing potions. Bella has almost finished the demon summoning area, and I have been creating a few reagents for that and brewing potions to buff myself during the fights. Bella has mentioned a beast called an "Elemental", and it has me slightly worried. A few new bruises later, and I now have a demon blood shard to call my own. I also have one procured by Magus to improve his ritual activation crystal with, and I will need to use a few reagents to merge the blood shard with the crystal, and some experimentation will be needed to find out what...

Hmm. It seems that the "Simple Catalyst" is the only alchemy reagent I could make with a Weak Blood Orb. Once I had the recipe (two parts Redstone, one part Glowstone, one part Sugar, and one part Gunpowder-mixing these together should make one Simple Catalyst), I placed one of each item in the outer five slots of the chemistry set. This alone is not enough to create a Simple Catalyst; you need to have a blood orb bound to you in the "Orb" slot to supply LP for the process (the Simple Catalyst only needs 200 LP, so it is fairly cheap). Tiberius mentioned he had already made a stronger blood orb, so I might ask him for help making my own. I'll log any recipes I find. With a bit of work, I have managed to create the other component of the tiny dark blue orb (the small light blue orb still eludes me; I might need to look into a stronger blood orb, but that will come later). The "Binding Agent" seems to have a few uses in both crafting and the other experiment I have been running with potions (more on that later). The Weak Binding Agent needs only two Simple Catalysts and a piece of Clay to form (along with 1k LP). I say weak because I feel I can improve it with some of the reagents I have been creating. For now, I should go over what I've made in the past month. With the help of Magus, I have managed to make "Alchemical Elemental Reagents." These reagents represent various elements found in the world that always play a major role in both magic and alchemy. I will make a quick list of each element and its recipes, and will try to create these entries as close to what I find in all the alchemy books I have read. Also, I should note that they all need 500 LP as a catalyst to make.

Magicales: Raw alchemical power seems to pulse in this dust, and I feel like I have only glimpsed the true potential of this reagent. I both fear and adore it. Made by mixing one part Redstone, one part Gunpowder, and two parts Glowstone in a Simple Catalyst.

Incendium: Holding the power of fire and the Nether, Incendium needs items often attributed to fire and that are a part of the Nether. Due to this, it is very hot and has left me with a few small burns from my time handling it.

Aether: A reagent holding the power of wind, I have had to make sure it doesn't float away with every breeze. It is made with items that seem to always be used in reference to wind (ghast tears and feathers) that I bound to Glowstone dust and a Simple Catalyst to give it some physical form.

Sanctus: The closest thing to powered light I could make, it seems to hold strange properties that I still can't understand. It needed a little gold, Glowstone dust, and glass I had ground up in the chemistry set to make, but it seems worth the cost.
Crepitous: Chaos and destruction in physical form, I named it after the creepers that gave me the idea (and the Gunpowder) for it. Made with one Simple Catalyst, two Cobblestone, and two Gunpowder.

Crystallos: A fine, cold powder that sends chills down my spine every time I touch it. Made with two parts ice (I need to find a better way to get this; the village doesn't have much in stock, and I burn through most of it trying to get the formula right), two parts snow (full blocks, not balls or sheets), and the standard Simple Catalyst.
Terrae: A hard, grainy powder that holds the power of the earth. Composed of two parts Obsidian, one part dirt, one part sand, and mixed together with a Simple Catalyst.

Aquasalus: A reagent that seems to shift between powder and liquid on a whim, representing the force of water in alchemy. Made by mixing three parts water (the amount in water bottles seems perfect), an ink sack (I didn't ask Magus why he has a huge stockpile of these in his storeroom, and he doesn't seem the type to mention it on a whim), and a Simple Catalyst.

Tennebrae: If Sanctus is solid light, Tennebrae is hardened shadow. Black as night and seems to dim everything around it, this reagent has potential to be powerful if used correctly. Made with Obsidian, two pieces of coal, a ball of Clay, and a Simple Catalyst.

My name is Vlad Highborn, and I am a Blood Mage. I have studied the intricate workings of alchemy and the process of "Equivalent Exchange", which governs all aspects of magic. Basically, you cannot create something from nothing, although many have tried when searching for a particular stone. That obviously didn't end well, because people are clamoring for a fake variant even today. Of course, simply saying that I am an alchemist isn't enough, because one of the main things I do is study Blood Magic with The Ritual Master and The Architect, both of whom have achieved those titles by their own merits. Magus and Tiberius have been busy recording their own works over the years, although I don't think Magus has everything written down in a book-I have yet to find any actual proof. Demir and me were working with a trading company named the "Merry Lamb", which operated throughout the lands traveling from place to place, selling our wares from horseback and buying whatever was of value. We didn't have last names, we didn't need them-the only thing of worth to the caravan company was how much profit you were able to obtain, and last names only got in the way of a sale. When we weren't busy with the various villages, trying to part with our gleaming swords and precious gems, all that was left for us was to read the many books that we obtained in the light through the canvas of the caravan. That was how I fell in love with alchemy in the early days. One of the members of the trading caravan I worked with was an alchemist, who created simple potions and poisons for both medical use and profit. He taught me many things while he worked with us, but I quickly learned that he only knew the basics of what could be done. This void of knowledge led me to collect several alchemical tomes from the merchants of passing villages, where I heard of a powerful mage that lived on the outskirts of a small village. At times I fantasized about meeting him, perhaps even learning alchemy like nothing I could ever dream of. But every rumor made me think he was more myth than man, filled with outrageous stories of his skill and power that no one else had ever come close to. Paired with the fact that no one had ever seen him almost killed the last of my dreams. I was reading the latest book in my collection, one that I bought from a hermit alchemist in the last village who kept muttering about turnips, when I noticed a flickering that didn't match the light of the candle I had in the caravan. I looked out of the back of the caravan as it slowed to a crawl; all the traders were looking at the same thing: a trail of dark smoke rising from behind the trees and blowing in the harsh wind. The head of the caravan quickly dispatched a group containing one person of each profession, which included myself as the now only alchemist, and we headed towards where the village used to stand. A massacre. I saw the smoke and ashes of the buildings, charred and even frozen flesh littering the ground. I swallowed heavily, looking around me for hope that I wouldn't lose my supper, and overheard someone speaking the obvious: "It must have been demons! No mage would use both ice and fire to attack a village." "Hell, no self-respecting mage would attack a village in the dead of night. They still honour that code from the medieval era." We readied our weapons, myself relegated to medic duty, but there was hardly any use because demons rarely stayed for more than an hour after they were done. "Hey", Nick shouted, a new member to our group, "there's someone here!" We all looked around and saw a little girl, possibly about age twelve, wandering through the ashes and looking both lost and dazed. "The demons leave no survivors, boy", the leader of our group said. "It is a bad omen to find her here, alive and alone. Hell," he laughed bitterly, starting to walk away, "that may not even be a - could be another demon for all we know." The thought stirred me, not of what she could be but that someone could leave a lost child by herself. "Fine," I said, after arguing the point for several minutes, "if you won't take her, I will leave the Merry Lamb." I can't fully remember the argument because of how much time passed before I could finally write it down. What I do remember is that the head of the caravan was quite startled at my proclamation, but finally agreed to send a carrier to fetch both my brother as well as my belongings, and to give me a good deal on some supplies. "I won't try to talk you out of it, since I know how you get when your mind is set. But if I may ask, why are you so intent on trying to help her?" I turned around to start walking towards the girl, who was watching us blankly. Not surprising, considering we were probably the first people she had seen today. Living, at least. After walking the few paces that put me between the girl and the caravan, I turned to the leader and said what I was holding onto for the past few years. "I know what it is like to not have any home to call my own. I'm hoping that this is not a bad omen, but rather a sign of fate." Unfortunately, it might have been a little preemptive of me to throw away my whole livelihood and wayward home to help a single lost girl. Demir wasn't exactly happy having to pick up everything he had to head out on an adventure and neither of us were expecting this, but I couldn't really blame him. Demir was attuned to several forms of magic, being the resident wizard-in-training of our group. Thankful for the little spark of mana that he managed to cultivate over the years, he kindled a fire for the three of us once we managed to walk off the rest of the night. Her name was Bella, with light blonde hair and blue eyes. When we asked her what happened that night, she simply shook her head and tucked her knees under her chin. Demir and I looked at each other, and we knew that no form of magic we knew would heal her of the wounds she had in her mind. When we tried to ask her if she knew of any magic herself, considering that we neared the border to the Mage's Guild's land, she shook her head again and looked sullenly back towards the village she came from, now miles behind us. Demir finally asked the question I was thinking myself-it seemed that he always had the uncanny ability to read my thoughts, or at least my mood at any given moment. "So, which way is it to this 'Magus Arcana?'" It was a long and difficult trek towards the village that the Mage was rumored to live in. Three long, blistering weeks. It is actually quite amazing how a distance can be so hard to traverse on foot without a caravan, pulling our dwindling belongings with us as we continued onwards towards our goal. When we reached a village, we would do the same thing: go to the local market at daybreak and sell whatever books and gems we could, grab our allotment of food for the next leg of the journey, and ask in the tavern if anyone had heard of rumors of the great mage Magus. It seemed that with each village our supplies were getting less prosperous, dwindling until all that was left was a few worthless rocks that no one was keen on buying. Thankfully, it seemed that we were getting close, since the rumors were becoming more and more substantial, until it became a reality. Passing by a blacksmith's shop, I noticed that the furnace was burning a lot more brightly than if it were filled with lava, and I peered into the slot for the fuel. What appeared to be there was a crystal made of lava, pulsating slowly as if it received a beat from a heart nearby. I asked the blacksmith about it, and he told me about an apprentice who made it, who didn't appear to have a name in the blacksmith's memory-if I were to hazard a guess, I'd say that he was more afraid of the apprentice than he let on. Grabbing Demir, who bought some antiseptic for a few wounds we received from a stray skeleton the previous night, and Bella, we finally headed towards the outskirts of the village we were looking for. The home wasn't hard to find; there was a simple Cobblestone path leading away from the village to a lone stone house. Considering the fact that there can't be that many homes out here like this, this was the place-or whoever does live here can give us directions to the right one. We walked up to the surprisingly simple wooden door, and I turned to the other two. "Are you ready?" I asked them, more for my sake than theirs. Bella simply nodded, barely speaking more than a few sentences a day since we left three weeks ago. Demir put his hand on my shoulder saying, "This is the place, right? Let's not just stand here like a bunch of geese." Gathering myself, I knocked three times on the door. At first, I feared we had the wrong house. Then I feared we had the right house, but no one was home... Before my mind could think of another scenario, I heard the sounds of a door being opened and someone walking on stone. The door swung inwards with a light squeak from the hinges, revealing someone of about eighteen wearing long robes. "Hello, how may I help you?" he asked after quickly looking us over, and I assumed this is the apprentice the blacksmith mentioned. "We're looking for the great mage Magus Arcana, is he here?" The man looked at all of us, then turned his head yelling, "Master, there is someone here to see you. They're asking for you by name." We soon heard a door open again, and a man who looked to be in his late thirties appeared behind the apprentice. I saw him briefly look the three of us over, raising his eyebrow as he did so. "You must be Magus. We've come a long way to meet you. May we come in?" He seemed to think this over for a few seconds, then sighed saying, "Alright, you may come in. Leave your boots at the door, then follow me to the main room. Tiberius, can you make a quick lunch for the five of us?" The apprentice nodded, then left around a corner to the right while Magus led us left to a large room with a few chairs, a simple couch, a plain wooden table, and an unlit fireplace with a strange red rock on the bottom. He gestured for the three of us to take a seat on the couch, which we gladly accepted. We had been on our feet for the last three weeks, so a chance to sit in a cool room was a nice change of pace. As Tiberius brought out a tray with several sandwiches on it to set on the table, I looked around the room to see what was on the walls. Stone tablets with strange symbols, brightly colored wands and staves adorned the walls like kings use old swords, and a small bookshelf was set above the fireplace holding a variety of books in a few languages. I recognized "The Theory of Equivalent Exchange" by Pahimar, the book that sparked the search for that certain stone. I noticed that while I had been gawking at the walls, everyone else had started eating. I grabbed the remaining sandwich, a simple pork and cheese with a strange sauce that I didn't recognize but immediately loved. "So..." Magus said as we finished the last few crumbs of the meal, "...what brings you to me?" Demir gave me a sideways glance, my cue to start talking. "Well, I heard stories of how much you know. I wanted to learn alchemy, so I came here. I know of only one other alchemist, the one who taught me the basics." He frowned, pinning his glare on me. "It looks like you three traveled a long way to get here, and you were unprepared for a long journey. So I'll ask again, what made you come to me?" I knew we didn't have much of a choice, so there was no point in lying. "My brother and I lived with traders. About three weeks ago we came across a village that was attacked by demons, with only one survivor." Magus glanced over at Bella, who was eating a second sandwich Tiberius had brought for us. "Yes, Bella was that survivor. Those other traders wanted to leave her for dead, but I couldn't bring myself to do that. So I was forced to go through with a plan I had been preparing for the last few years, trying to find you early. I had originally planned to come here alone, and had just enough money to get one person here. We barely scraped by with three, getting here with the last few gems I had to trade." Magus nodded, an intense look on his face. "And what were you planning to do if I was not here, or you never found me, or if I was a myth like many people think I am? Or did you even have a plan?" I sighed at his questions; he really pinned me down and read me like a book. "I had a backup plan, if a bad one. If worse came to worst, I planned on trying to find a village that needed an alchemist to brew potions. I still have all the equipment in my bag, one of the few things I couldn't bring myself to sell. I know how much the traders made off my work; I could feed the three of us with it, if only just barely." Magus nodded as if I gave the right answer. "Now then, what of your brother and your friend Bella? What had you planned to do with them if you found me?" "Well, my brother has a little mana, enough to create sparks strong enough to light fires. As for Bella, she doesn't know if she has any talent for magic." Magus's gaze shifted over to Demir, then Bella, then returned to me. "And if your brother or Bella didn't have enough talent for me to teach them?" I sighed once again. He was asking all the right questions. "I would shift to plan B. I'm not leaving my brother or Bella, not after all we have been through, and not for the teachings of a heartless mage." He gave me a hard stare for a few seconds, then a wide grin grew on his face as he said, "Right answer. Alright, I'll see what I can do. I should be able to teach something to you three, and I doubt anyone else around here is going to take her in. Rumors of the blond-haired demon girl have beaten you here." Magus made a few arrangements for us, having Demir and me stay in Tiberius's room while Bella took Magus's. When I asked where he would be sleeping, Magus said he kept the old couch around for more than one reason. When I started to protest he said that this was only temporary and that the three of us would have our own rooms tomorrow. When I asked how, all he did was smile and say, "You'll see." While the three of us got accustomed to our new home, Magus and Tiberius went out for a few things. "Well, they're an odd bunch", Demir said shortly after they left. "Don't laugh, they can say the same about us", I told him. This comment earned a rare smile from Bella, who had slowly started coming out of her shell. Magus and Tiberius returned a little over an hour later, Magus carrying a huge amount of food while Tiberius had a large roll of uncut fabric. Magus brought the food to the main room we sat at before; its intoxicating smell had caused both my brother and Bella to start drooling. I would criticize them if I wasn't doing the same thing. "Even after lunch, you three looked half-starved", Magus said as he set down loaves of fresh bread, cheese, and dried meat slices. "So we got you something, though we didn't have many options on short notice. Consider it a welcoming gift, along with some new clothes we'll make. But those can come later; for now, you can dig in!" We ate like wilder beasts, tearing apart the bread, clawing for the meat, and making sure to get every last crumb of the cheese. I had no idea just how hungry I was till I saw all that food, and by the end of it I was amazed at how long it had been since I ate like this. Three weeks ago? No, a few months ago. When the traders were celebrating a huge trade with a large and wealthy village, the leader was so happy that he almost spent half the money he earned off the deal on the party. Almost. After a nice long night of sleep, we all awoke to the sounds of Magus and Tiberius carving out a large chunk of the dirt on the other side of a wall. I was fascinated by how they were doing it: Magus cast a spell to remove the dirt, then Tiberius replaced the dirt with stone bricks using a strange looking wand. At first, I wondered where all the dirt was going and stone was coming from, then I noticed a few strange bags at the side of Magus and Tiberius. Once the main size was laid out, Magus asked Tiberius for the bag he had. With it in hand, Magus raised one arm to have walls raise out of the ground with it. Then Tiberius grabbed a few strange flying flames to light up the hallways, and candles for the rooms. "Alright, we're done. You three now have rooms to call your own. I'll have to do some work, but we might be able to get a few beds here as well. I only have one spare, so you three can decide who gets it for now." "Bella", my brother and I said in unison. "Alright. Tiberius, can you give me a hand moving it to her room? Also, your rooms have a small work area. If you need more space, you can use the main basement area or let us know. We'll see what we can do. For now, you three can pick which room you want, then move and unpack your things there." The next two days went by fast; Magus helped make our rooms homes and assisted us in finding fields of magic to study (he had over a dozen tomes on alchemy inside his huge library, so I quickly felt at home with my nose in a book). While he attended to Demir and Bella, I started digging into the tomes. After cross-referencing several of the books, I noticed that very few ever tried to improve upon the first brewing stand. Of the few who did, none succeeded in making potions larger than one dose. After briefly talking with Magus and Tiberius, they encouraged me to try and improve the design and gave me a space in the main workroom to do my testing.

I knew I needed to try and reinforce the stand, as it was far too fragile to mix more than one item at a time. I tried iron, gold, stone, and several other materials. They either were far too weak, incompatible with the stand, or unruly with my attempts to shape them. It was when I tried to use Obsidian, something compatible with the stand and strong enough to withstand the strain of the alchemy process. My only problem was fusing the Obsidian with the stand. While I pondered my options, I felt my hand brush against a strange red orb that had been sitting next to my workspace. Once I did so, the Obsidian seemed to spring to life, wrapping around and shaping the stand into something far greater. I called down Magus and Tiberius to see what just happened. When Magus asked how I did what many others had failed at, I told him the truth. "I'm not sure. I was thinking of how to do just this, when I accidentally touched something on that table and then the Obsidian sprang to life." "You touched something and the Obsidian seemed to come to life? What did you..." Magus said, then stopped dead as he looked at the other table. "Was it that orb?" he asked hastily. "I think so. After I touched it, this happened. It looks like what I created had a slot shaped like that orb." I told him, and Magus looked shaken. "Tiberius, we're going to need to talk about this. For now, Vlad, can you hold off on testing what that device does?" "Alright", I told him, a little confused. "But I think I should name it. How does 'The Alchemical Chemistry Set' sound?" Magus put on a weak smile. "That seems fitting. It seems to be much more than a simple brewing stand. I recall Demir saying you had a few alchemical items that an adventurer sold to the traders in your possession. Perhaps you can try to work out what they do, or what they're made of." Trying what Magus suggested, I started experimenting with the strange alchemy items I collected in my time with the traders. In total, I had two small red orbs, one larger red item that seemed like a better version of the red orb, three small blue orbs, and two blue items that seemed to be between the small orbs and the large ones. Using a small alchemy lab Magus brought me to, I started breaking down anything I had spares of. Taking one of the blue orbs and grinding it in a mortar and pedestal, I found it was made of three Redstone and two items I had never seen before. One was acting as a "Binding" agent, while the other was some sort of liquid catalyst. After a few hours of work, I had a few formulas for the items, but I still needed to recreate them. Normal mixing wasn't working, as it seems like there was some other factor that merged them in the first place that I am missing. I'll write the formulas here when I find out what I'm missing, so until then I start grinding up the other items. Alright, after about three days' worth of work, I have now discovered that my original assumption that the larger red and blue reagents were stronger, more "condensed" versions of the small orbs was correct. After a bit of work, I am starting to think there is some sort of link between the Alchemical Chemistry Set and these reagents. The chemistry set has five "Input" slots and one "Output" slot, and many of the items here need just five items... I will need to ask Magus about trying this with the orb that formed the set inside. Well, I am apparently now a blood mage. Magus and Tiberius told us details about some of the items we had been finding around our new home, from the Weak Blood Orb that helped create the Alchemical Chemistry Set (which Bella later used to tame her new demon friend; after everything I have heard about them, he is remarkably civil) to the altar behind the house and in the basement. I was given the choice of continuing to study blood magic and use my new chemistry set (and take all the risks that come with it), or studying other forms of alchemy. I went with the risky option, simply because I would be blazing a new form of magic. I now have a Weak Blood Orb to call my own, and I will start trying to experiment with creating some of the reagents I have discovered in the last few days.

>A note: this is an entry written several years after the others before and after this. After talking to the others, I am adding this here as a postscript to aid others who read this for the simple reason of "We would have loved to have this when we were starting out." This will, however, mention people and items that might be foreign to you for now. Roll with it; it will all make sense later.<

I have found something... well, unexpected to say the least. The self-proclaimed hedge mage Athis stopped by our still-in-construction homestead in Venric's Folly to visit Tiberius. Apparently, in one of the letters he wrote her, he mentioned being unable to relax after working on watching the demons running around and building various things he and Magus decided we needed here (isn't this meant to be a temporary base of operations?). She came by with a small pouch of wood ash incense and a little brazier to help him with this, but what this provided was far more valuable than simple scented air. I joined Tiberius and Athis for the first use of the incense, and to her credit, I started feeling relaxed breathing in the sweet scents it let off. Partway through, I got up to visit the blood altar, being my turn in the roster to top out the communal soul network. After performing a sacrifice like normal, something odd happened: there was more LP in the altar than there should be, by a fair margin. Several sacrifices later, I couldn't get it to happen again, so I went in to mention it to Tiberius. (While it might have been a simple miscalculation, we must always look deeper into it. This philosophy was passed down to us by Magus and has saved us time, led us to great discoveries like this, and at times has resulted in a lot of cheese). He performed his own sacrifice in the altar, and again there was more LP than there should be. Long story short, involving investigations into the local flora, positions of stars, and phases of the moon, we discovered it was the incense of all things causing the discrepancy. As it turns out, being under the effects of this simple wood ash resulted in a greater exchange of raw life essence for a given amount of blood, akin to how self-sacrifice runes work. After some experimentation, we have a basic calculation for the process and method for the most profit. You must sit in range of the improved brazier I designed after giving it wood ash until white particles are emitted (you can do the sacrifice before this, but you won't get the full effect). You then must sacrifice almost all of your blood in one quick burst (achieved by holding right-click for several seconds, then releasing). LP will then be added to the altar based on the number of hearts sacrificed, plus the bonus of the self-sacrifice runes in the altar. This total is then multiplied by the effect of the highest quality incense you are under. Example: if you sacrifice nine hearts into an altar without any self-sacrifice runes while under the full effect of wood ash, you would add 2160 LP to the altar instead of the normal 1800. This process isn't without issues, however, as this rapid expenditure of blood weakens you for a time, with an effect not unlike soul fray.

Now then, I mentioned "Highest quality incense" before. Well, after the revelation that mundane wood ash would offer a sizeable boon to LP creation, I descended into my lab to perfect the process by creating better incense. After three days, ten pots of coffee, and one nap I emerged with four new incenses: Byrrus, Livens, Viridis, and Purpura for bonuses to LP creation of 60%, 120%, 200%, 300% respectively, compared to the 20% of wood ash. There is a minor issue, however: You can't just make and use the strongest one and be done with it. You see, these are designed to be used with each other and wood ash in a sort of chain. Once you reach the peak of wood ash, Byrrus can start taking effect, once you are at it's peak Livens can start, and so on. I should also note that while the LP gains they offer are improved, the relative scents they can let off vary from par with the wood ash to as foul as a compost pile. Sacrifices must be made, and a few foul fumes is worth the gains. I should note that you can speed up the process by which you are effected by increasing the volume of vapours inhaled. In laymans terms, the more braziers active with the same incense around you the faster the effect can take hold.

It has been a week since we ironed out most of the kinks with the reagent system, and Magus brought all of us together around the dinner table to go over the next few months. He said that he could get us something he felt would be needed to upgrade the altar to tier five, but it would take a little over a year to get them. He also mentioned that we should be getting a few messages after this year's Hell Harvest Festival, which I thought was a little odd. "A little odd" doesn't begin to describe what has been happening the last few days. It seems most of us have put research aside while we watch some of the "Replies" come in. They have come in via airdrop, mechanized mail carriers, train, and countless other ways that always seem stranger than the last. Tiberius managed to ask Magus what this was all about, and he simply replied that he invited a few guests over, and these were the replies they had sent. When pressed for more details, he just said they wouldn't be coming for a few months, so we should start mastering what we can do with our blood orbs. We then started showing each other the little details of the branches of blood magic we had created and had been perfecting. In the last few months I have befriended a few demons with the help of my sister, created a few spell crystals and helped construct a large complex spell with my brother, and then forged armor and sigils with Tiberius. Then it came time to teach the others alchemy and potion brewing... I was reluctant to give out my secrets to brewing potions, even to them. I had told no one the recipes for these brews, brewing potions for the others myself when they needed them. I almost wanted to tell the others no, but then Magus made me an offer. "I understand how you want to keep the secrets of your brews hidden, so how about we make a trade of knowledge instead?" he asked me when I was contemplating this matter. He offered me details about himself, something that wasn't common knowledge, and even gave me permission to write everything down. Considering how little I knew of him, even after all these years, I quickly took him up on this offer. The very next day I had everyone in my personal lab, showing them the details and reciting the recipes for some of the most potent effects I had found, then demonstrating their uses. I was done showing them everything shortly before dinner, so while we ate in the common room, Magus told us his story. I'll jot as much of it as I can recall here, for you to enjoy as well. "So it is time to tell my story... I always hate doing this. So many questions that I really don't have answers for, and frankly it is a long bloody story. But a deal is a deal, and you all deserve to hear it. I have only told a handful of people this, all of them were either mages or Conglomeration members. You will so count among this number... I was born in the middle of the Talus Kingdom, before all these corporations were founded and started forming their own governments. Back then gods and kings dictated law, and wars were fought on the battlefield and not in market shares and advertisement campaigns. My family was small; all I had was a mother who did all she could at home and a father who worked at the royal library. I ended up spending many hours in that library, both helping my father with his work and studying the countless tomes that adorned those shelves. At an early age I discovered a hidden treasure trove in those shelves: books on magic. At the time magic wasn't well known, and most regarded it as nothing but myths created by fools. Because of this, these books stayed lost and forgotten on these shelves until I came along. While other boys were learning the right way to hold a sword or a pickaxe, I spent my time studying the arcane. At the end of my first year there, I had already created a basic fireball spell and a Thaumanonicon. I managed to keep my activities in magic hidden from everyone, my parents included, until I had come of age and needed to find a profession. It was then that I told them of what I had been working on all those years, showing them some of the smaller tricks I had perfected. To say they were shocked is an understatement, so I felt it best to leave their little world in the kingdom and set out to find a new home to practice magic without needing to be as secretive. That is how I came to Lurric, and it has been my home ever since then. The early days were hard, as I really didn't have the funds to live off of, let alone support my research. I managed to get by helping the locals: merchants with bookkeeping and identifying some of the more obscure relics and "treasures" they had for sale, farmers with stock and management, and even as a cook when times were really dark for me. But this only lasted a year or two, then I had the infrastructure in place to support myself with a little extra to live on. Amazing how much traders are willing to spend on floating balls of flame and purple metal... Skipping ahead a few years through the dull portion, I had begun to master a few forms of magic like thaumurgy and botany. My name had started to spread to the other nearby villages, and people asking for favors and knowledge started popping up at my door like they do now. At the time I never asked for gifts or compensation, but I didn't turn down food or books if they were offered. Traders started traveling to Lurric more and more, hoping to acquire a few goods that only I could provide at the time in exchange for gold, jewels, and rare books. Those who brought the third I gave the best deals. Still, life went on like this for a few more years, with books starting to pile up in my library, more than enough gold to pay for my more "exotic" materials, and never having a day of rest for the full decade I had first lived here. That peace was shattered the day a man by the name of Gareth broke down my door. He came in, adorned in full iron armor and longsword in hand, to challenge me to a duel to the death. It took more than a few sleep spells to knock him out of his rage, at which point I restrained him to a reclined chair I had in the back that I used when treating the wounded. When he finally awoke, I started interrogating him. Well, interrogate isn't quite the right word for it... Honestly, I just asked him a few questions. Once I saw that he had calmed down, I untied him and offered food. Did I mention the sounds his stomach made while he was unconscious? They were strong enough to rattle the chair. After eating a whole bread loaf and a large part of the stew I had been preparing before he arrived, we sat in this very room to talk like civil beings over why he decided to break down my door. His story is about as ludicrous as mine is. He was one of fifty-seven immortal beings who walked the earth. He told me what details he could, but he seemed unsure about it as well. What he did tell me was that the gift of immortality comes with a few boons aside from the obvious, and what they are differs from person to person. He said his gift was that of prophecy, and he recently had a vision of the future where I and people I influence would play a major role. As a result, he came here to challenge me to a duel to the death. I then asked him if that wasn't a bit unfair, him being immortal and all. He, in the most serious tone possible, said that it was completely fair: While an immortal cannot be killed normally, there are set ways that it can happen. One way is by a one-on-one duel to the death, with immortality wagered as the prize. They really don't have much choice in this, as it is like natural magic: The mere act of the duel happening is enough for the "wager" to take place. If both parties exert their full strength, then the killing blow is enough to complete the wager and transfer the gift. We talked for the next few hours, and I learned quite a few interesting facts. He had no idea who the other fifty-six immortals were, and he frankly had no way to tell them apart from normal humans. He also mentioned that he could still be injured outside of the duel, but he would not fall to mortal wounds and would heal at an accelerated rate-not much of one, however, as he mentioned breaking a leg once and it taking over a month to fully heal. Another note was how short a time he had been immortal; he had gained it about two decades ago. While to you that seems like a long time, he said the one he killed was alive for over a century. We finally ended that night with an agreement: In one week's time he would return to my home, where we would share a fine meal, then have our duel the next morning. He wanted to get straight to the duel, but I had the meal as a non-negotiable point that he finally caved on. I spent the next week preparing for the battle, arming myself with the most potent spells and artifacts at my disposal from several schools of magic. In a flash that week went by, then Gareth once again sat with me to eat at my table. I gave him a bed to sleep in that night, then at dawn we both walked to the hill just behind this house where Bella's garden currently lays. Of all things about Gareth, our battle is one thing I barely remember. Once we reached the top of the hill, we both drew our blades and turned to each other. After that, I only remember flashes and out-of-order scenes. It felt like it was over in only a few minutes, but it might have been hours and was one of the most brutal fights I have ever been a part of. His agility was far greater than I expected, dodging my swings and spells with ease. Unfortunately for him, I was still a force to be reckoned with back then. I never let up on my spells, casting fire, ice, and lightning one after another using my foci, then teleporting around with a few spells. In the end, he died when he dropped his sword in reflex to the heat my flame spell had left on it, and I capitalized on this. By this point, we both felt taxed by the fight, and he could barely avoid my slowest attacks. The final blow I dealt was out of mercy, a quick end for his suffering that I had caused. I watched as Gareth grinned at me like he knew this would be how he died, then he closed his eyes as his body turned into sand carried away in the wind. I fell to my side after that, strength sapped and mana depleted, to awake a few hours later. I felt a new strength in my body when I got up, slight but still there. All in all, suddenly having immortality was rather lackluster, but that was how it happened." At this point I was shocked into silence at his words-not what he said, but how he said them: little feeling or emphasis. It was like he just said that he gained a new scar or it started to rain. He has been more emotional over the acquisition of a rare book than immortality. Glancing at the others, I could tell they were mulling over this information as well. After a few minutes, my brother spoke up to start the questions. "So... Did your life change much after that?" Demir asked Magus, before taking a bite out of a sandwich he seemed to have created from thin air. "Not really. Life as an immortal was just the same as life as a mortal. More researching, more learning, more magic." "Have you met any more immortals since then?" Bella asked. "Two, and I happen to be related to both of them." "Related?" asked Tiberius with curiosity, "I never knew you had any relatives." "Well, they never came up. One of them is my brother, who started studying the Myst a few decades ago and hasn't been heard from since. I expect he will pop by anytime he feels homesick for a few days, then drop out of touch again." "And the other immortal?" Bella asked with interest. "The other is my wife." Once again we all went into stunned silence, Tiberius and Demir slack-jawed. "You're married! Since when?" Bella asked after a moment. "A few centuries ago. We met when a small war was being fought with a necromancer, and she was the one leading the forces. Of course, most people at the time didn't know her real gender. She tried hard to keep it hidden, so the troops wouldn't think of her any differently. I was brought in to help deal with the "Undead army" details of the whole thing, and that had me working with her. One thing led to another, and we were married a few months after the war was over. Currently she works as a commander of the Conglomeration's defense force, so she rarely has time to come home." The questions continued for the next half hour, ranging from "Did you really open the first Nether Portals?" to "Why are you on the Conglomeration board?" Magus took all our questions with the air of a man who has done this all before. When the questions were over, all the others started retiring to their rooms while I stopped by the library to look up something. The Talus Kingdom fell almost a millennium ago. Wow... It has been a few months since I last wrote in this book. I've met more people in the last few weeks than I have in the last few years, many of them from lands I have never set foot in! Kings and queens, rulers and underlords, CEOs and owners from every nation. Then there was the fight with the Withers... I'm not sure what to say about all that. I sort of walked in there, chugged a few potions, then let the years of training with Magus take over. By the time the adrenaline rush was over for me, we had killed all of the Withers, and I was barely aware of a dull pain in my leg. Magus has used a spell to restrict my movement so I won't leave this bed while my broken leg heals, since I "may" have tried to sneak into my lab once or twice to get to work. For now, I must be content with my notebook and what Magus brings me from his library to pass the days...

After a few weeks worth of work, I finally managed to upgrade the binding agent and have made one that lets me make more advanced potions with more then one effect. Unfortunately, it doesn't work every time. For the first effect it works every time, like the Weak Binding Agent. For the second effect, it only works four times out of ten(On average). Then the third effects works only sixteen times out a hundred(Again, on average.) It also needs 1.5K LP to make the binding agent when mixing a Weak Binding Agent, a Sanctus and a Crystallos. With how rare some of the ingredients of my potions are, I decided to create a "Filling agent" that replaces the solution in the potion flask so that I can get more uses out of them. I have noticed that potions with more then one effect require stronger filling agents, as every effect in the potion cuts down how effective the agent is. The Weak Filling Agent is made with a Simple Catalyst, a pile of Redstone and Glowstone dust, and a piece of nether wart. The Weak Filling Agent can then be upgraded with a Terrae and 1K LP into a "Standard" filling agent.

That is it for the reagents, for now. The other use for the alchemical chemistry set I have found is the creation of potions unlike anything anything I have ever seen. While not big on taste(But really, has there ever been a potion that isn't hard to swallow?), the potions it makes are more... refined. Using a single flask(Made in a T2 blood altar with2K and a glass bottle, the first being made by accident when I dropped the bottle in the lab after tripping on a table leg that had been moved), a potion ingredient, and a binding agent I can turn the solution in the flask(A mixture of nether wart, Redstone, and Glowstone dust) into a potion that has eight uses or "Swigs" instead of the normal one per bottle. Another interesting power of these new potions is that the red and blue alchemy items I had acquired from the adventures(Who in turn got from some chest in a dungeon) can be used to "Augment" the potions by mixing them in with more of potions ingredient. The red ones I have dubbed "Power catalysts", making the potions effect much more potent at the cost of shortening the effect. The blue ones I have started calling "Lengthening catalysts", as they make the potions last much longer then normal. On another note, I have started trying to make a better binding catalyst after an idea came to me from a mishap in the lab. I had tried to make a slowness potion(We had a few villagers that had been pestering us, so I wanted to get rid of them without hurting them), but after adding in the Sugar powered I tried mixing in a fermented spider eye. Trying to add it in with a weak binding catalyst, I noticed that instead of mixing with the speed potion it was forming it's own section the same color of a weakness potion. Then the flask exploded. If my theory holds true, these potions can hold more then one effect, but the solution destabilizes when an effect is added. Should the potion fully destabilize, it will cause a small explosion that shatters the flask and damages anyone close to it with the glass shards. If I can help keep the potion stable, I might have found a secret of alchemy countless mages have sought but never found...

I have been experimenting with what I can make with this new blood orb, a gift from Tiberius for my help with his sigils. Using this orb I have finally been able to recreate the power and lengthening catalyst. Sadly, I can only make the mundane versions of each, but one step at a time. I haven't actually made many new items for my potions and alchemy(Well, compared to the shift from weak to apprentice orbs) but everything I have found is extremely useful with my potions. Then there is what I've been making for my brother, but I wrote most of the uses of them in his book. I'll add the recipes here anyway, for completeness sake.

The first step towards these new reagents was to make a better form of catalyst. Surprisingly, this was the easy part. By mixing in a netherwart and bonemeal into two simple catalysts, I could create two "Strengthened catalyst" with which to create new reagents and enhance old ones.

Shortly after this discovery, I managed to make a reagent I have dubbed "Offensa" by mixing in two arrows, a flint, and a strengthened catalyst into an Incendium. While the original reagents represented elements, these new reagents seem to represent ideas and concepts(With "War and battle" being given to offensa).

More tinkering gave birth to Praesidium, which seems to represent "Defense and protection" and is created by mixing tennibrae into strengthened catalyst, iron ingot(Ground into a powder at the set), Redstone dust, and a cobweb(This may or may not have fallen into the set when Bella was doing some cleaning, ending with this happy accident).

By strengthening Terrae with the better catalyst, sand, gun powder, and a Netherrack chunks(Luckily, we still have some from the last hell harvest festival but I must remember to buy more in a few months), I have created orbis Terrae. Where Terrae seems to be the element of earth, orbis Terrae is the environment itself, encompassing above and below ground from the dessert to the nether.

After a few days of nothing, I managed to form a powder now called "Virtus" from two parts Redstone, one part coal, and one part gun powder mixed into a strengthened catalyst. From what I can tell, this is the raw manifestation of power(Fitting, this reagent is hard to control and a few of our uses of it have backfired horribly). It holds in it a great deal of potential energy, but releasing it(And then controlling it) has proven to be very difficult.

This next one is a little odd. Late one night in the lab I had been mixing things together to see the results, and something caused me to mix a gold ingot powdered in the stand, soul sand from our nether wart farm, Redstone dust, and a carrot of all things in the strengthened catalyst. When I awoke the next day, I found three things: A reagent called Reductus(The aspect of reduce and diminish), a large mess in the lab, and that this wasn't the strangest things I had mixed together. Since then I have started brewing pots of coffee before I begin working late in an attempt to stay lucid.

The final reagent that I have created is called "Potentia", due to the energy that causes it to crackle and pop on its own(Note: As my brother accidentally discovered, this powder does have some electrical properties to it that caused his hair to stand on end when he was working with it). Created with two chunks of lapis lazuli, Glowstone dust, a piece of nether quartz, and a strengthened catalyst, this powder is similar to virtus. The difference is that while virtus is raw power, potentia is energy. Ironically, virtus is the more stable of the two, only giving off energy in large bursts while potentia seems to give off a little at all times.

It has taken the last two months, but we have the groundwork for testing our idea done. The results so far have been even better than expected. We have only tested the full Spring ritual and have discovered quite a few effects, but I'll let Magus cover those.

Instead, I'll write how the reagent system works. You first need an Alchemic Calcinator, then place a Blood Orb into it to act as a power source. After that, reagents can be placed by hand or fed into the Calcinator to turn into pure alchemical energy, the type based on the reagent fed in. Once it has a solid reagent, it will use LP to turn one reagent into 1000 AR (Alchemy Reagent), which is then moved into the 2000 AR "Buffer" of the Calcinator. Once in the buffer, the reagent slowly starts being moved into the main tank, which can then be siphoned out.

Now then, to move it out of the main tank, you need to have somewhere for it to go. To this extent, you have three options: a Crystal Belljar, an Alchemic Relay, or a Master Ritual Stone. How you need to link it is simple: Create an Alchemic Router, then Shift-right-click with it on the Calcinator to select the reagent type for it to transport (a note for blocks with more than one tank and more than one reagent type: Shift-right-clicking again on the block will swap between the available reagents inside the block), then normal right-click on the block with the router to bind it to the block. After that, right-click on the destination (needs to be within a few blocks; the range isn't that large). If it has worked, you should see reagent "flowing" to the destination from the source (in this case, the Calcinator). We have tweaked it so you can't see reagent moving with the naked eye-you need to have a tool (like the Alchemic Router) in hand to see this effect. You can also use a Divination Sigil on the Belljars, Relays, Calcinator, and Master Ritual Stone to read how much reagent the device holds. This process of binding can be applied to all the other blocks, so I shouldn't need to cover it further, but I should note that these blocks can only accept and send reagent to a limited number of locations at once. For example, the Belljar can only accept reagent from one location, and send it to one location. I must also reiterate that if you have a Relay set to send Aether to destination A and Tennibrae to destination B, Aether can never travel to B, and vice versa for Tennibrae. New connections must be made for each reagent type, and we could not get a "colorless" version of a connection to function.

Getting more into detail about the blocks and items of our new system, I'll cover the Belljar first. Created out of mundane glass and wood slabs, then filled with a Concentrated Catalyst solution to contain the alchemical energy in a stable enough environment to allow you to move the jar without losing any energy inside. While it can hold only one type of reagent and is restricted to one source and one destination, it functions as a portable form of "bulk storage" (able to hold 16000 AR). An option for more storage is to link a few Belljars together, but I feel this is far from a perfect answer to the problem of mass storage of reagent... I will need to talk with Tiberius and Magus about this later. Regardless, Tiberius managed to incorporate a bit of Redstone interaction into the design of the jar. Based on the amount of reagent inside the jar, it outputs a Redstone signal (15 when full, 0 when empty, and so on). With a bit of work, you can use this for automated systems.

The "Alchemy Relay" acts as a small buffer (two tanks that can hold two reagents each) and can be used to merge and divide a transport line of reagent energy. Each relay can have limitless sources and four destinations. With the creative use of relays, you can create a large power network for transporting reagent. Tiberius has worked his magic on this device as well and tweaked it to not send reagent when a Redstone signal is applied (it also spins slightly slower to represent this).

To assist with the use of this system, we have three items to manage these devices. The Alchemic Router is used to bind the destinations of set reagents for all devices. The Alchemic Segmenter is used to partition tanks to a set reagent. All you need to do is set the reagent type the same way you would the router, then right-click the device you want to partition a tank for that reagent type. One tank will be set for that type per right-click, and if you exceed the maximum number of available tanks, it will reset all partitioned tanks to the default "first come, first served." I should also note that if you set a relay to accept Sanctus, Offensa, and Virtus, the two available tanks will be distributed to whichever reagents arrive first. The final item is the Alchemic Cleanser, and its use is simple but very useful: it resets all destinations. All locations the device is set to send reagent are cleared, so you can easily bind the device to new locations.

Now, we have made a few minor alterations to the "Master Ritual Stone" to enable our system to function. Its recipe and normal uses have remained the same, but it now has three internal tanks that each hold 1000 AR. If the ritual has any reagent, it will display an "Alchemy Ring" above the Master Ritual Stone as a sign that it has been augmented. Then, depending on the ritual and the effect in question, it will use an amount of reagent to perform a new effect or augment an old one. An example of this is the full Spring filled with Aquasalus, which will convert earth into farmland then hydrate it in a nine-by-nine area around the Master Ritual Stone, but if the full Spring is given Crystallus, it will freeze all water source blocks around it. This is all paired with the base effect of the rituals, so the full Spring can still function as an endless water source. This is all I can think of to write down about our new system. Tiberius and I plan to show it to the others tomorrow, so I need to get some rest. We showed our new system to Magus and my siblings today, and to say they loved it was an understatement. We had decided to be a little flashy with the show, building a full Spring next to a small pond that had formed from the recent rainfall. After a bit of work hiding the relays and the Belljar, Tiberius hid out of sight while I showed the others the demonstration. I asked Magus to activate the ritual, keeping a close eye to see if he focused on anything in particular, but he quickly and effortlessly activated the ritual without pausing for a moment. After he returned to my side, I yelled for Tiberius to throw the switch. In an instant, the reagent flowed to the ritual, and as the alchemy circle formed in the air, the water created by the ritual and that of the pond quickly froze over. I heard gasps from both of my siblings, and I noticed Magus's eyes widen for just a moment (his equivalent of a jaw hanging slack) before he composed himself. Afterwards, we went over the details for them of how it works for the others, explaining the minor modifications we had made to the basic Master Ritual Stone design and such.

I've only had a little time at my chemistry set, so I haven't had much time to experiment with my new orb. All my tests trying to make new reagents failed, and I so far have only managed to make two new runic slates for my brother (but we have been trying to find new uses for them). The normal runic slate is a simple upgrade to the old cracked slates by infusing Terrae into them. The final slate, dubbed imbued, is two runic slates bound together with Magicales, Incendium, and Aquasalus. These days I've been working with the others on a few secret projects, so I have needed to keep up with and research all kinds of strange subjects. I also always seem to need to make more reagents, as our experiments burn through them rather quickly... I will write more when I have the time.

I managed to find a new use for the weak blood shards that the others have been gathering. Since the shards are technically part of a "Soul", I tried mixing it in with a bucket of water and sand using my chemistry set to get a fairly close replication of an uncommon nether resource, soul sand. While not identical, it can serve the same purpose as the normal one found in the nether.

It just occurred to me, it has been over three years since I came to Magus's doorstep with my brother and sister. I've gotten so use to living here, and the daily routine seems like something I've done all my life. Strange, I never thought I'd settle down. Five years ago, I'd have never considered leaving the caravan. I have barely left my lab in the last month, aside from when Magus, my brother or sister drag me out by the back of my robe. Normally I would go out willingly, but we recently finished our altar upgrade and have created the "Master Blood orbs." As is customary, this new orb has given me the boost in power needed to create more alchemy items for both general use and my potions. As a result, progress has been coming in leaps and bounds with something new almost every other day. After many late nights and early mornings, theses are the fruits of my labor.

Moving my attention on to runes for our wonderful new altar, I had a revelation as I noticed a speed rune next to a dislocation rune: Increasing how much LP is moved from the buffer is fine, but how about increasing how often it transfers LP? Using a few materials like buckets and an ethereal slate, I have transformed a normal speed rune into something far greater.
